Sure. Just would like to complete the spec and collect my questions and concerns <@!203220829473996800> Updated Nethermind part with docker, official release and some refactoring: https://github.com/protolambda/mergenet-tutorial/pull/11 docker teku + docker nethermind on linux VM: https://github.com/protolambda/mergenet-tutorial > `go install github.com/protolambda/eth2-testnet-genesis@latest` I have go1.13.8 and I'm getting `go: cannot use path@version syntax in GOPATH mode` the docs say > Go 1.15 and lower did not support using version queries with go install. is go 1.16 or later a requirement? Go 1.16 is a requirement for the genesis tool yes. The val tools minimum is go 1.14 I recommend you update Go. The language has nice non-breaking releases, it should be really smooth. sure but I guess it should be mentioned then Will add it to the readme, thanks 👍 Also, that error about GOPATH mode is because older Go versions didn't go as far with the new go-modules support. Dependency management in Go was always a pain, but Go modules really improved it a lot. New Go versions do the right things by default there, I can't recommend updating enough. it's actually a fresh Ubuntu in WSL so I'm installing everything from scratch See https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/Ubuntu, the default golang package via APT may be outdated, but there are plenty of other ways to install it yeah I installed from the PPA now did you have to install wheel and dev packages before running `pip install -r requirements.txt`? mine failed with `invalid command 'bdist_wheel'` and `Python.h: No such file or directory` <@!132497957135187968> are you using a venv? In python it's common to mask your global environment with a "virtual environment", to install packages locally, per project. Venv support is just another python package. You can install it globally, and then use it to create venvs for projects, and install dependencies per-project, in a standard way. yeah I followed the instructions but got errors until I ran `pip install wheel` and `apt install python3-dev` Probably some binary dependency in the crypto related to the Web3 package. Those `wheel` and `python3-dev` are pretty standard, must be some quirk with your fresh Ubuntu install. > Configure tranche(s) of validators, edit eth2_genesis_validators.yaml. should it be genesis_validators.yaml? Ah yes, good catch > # Generate Genesis Beacon State > eth2-testnet-genesis merge \ does this assume that wherever go installs executables is in PATH? it seems this isn't the case by default yes, it assumes your `$HOME/go/bin` directory is in your PATH. Or you could run from source (git clone, `go run .`) it's a bit more complicated > Executables (main packages) are installed to the directory named by the GOBIN environment variable, which defaults to $GOPATH/bin or $HOME/go/bin if the GOPATH environment variable is not set. shame that it's not mentioned in https://golang.org/doc/install... Right, that's a shame. Anyway, happy to help with more details, but let's continue in DM to not spam here.

Quick call summary:
- Ethglobal talks, Nethermind, Prysm and researchers are all presenting. See above link ^
- Nimbus is working on Merge as well. Side-project: Nimbus eth1 fuzzing. Hypothetically, if Nimbus-eth1 implements EVM for all hardforks, and has a working DB model, and consensus RPC, it may be able to integrate merge before the Eth1 client finishes. Will use Catalyst (Geth) during next month though.
- Nethermind and Lighthouse part of mergenet-tutorial now

- Testnet plan: 1 day testnet first, test interop. Proto will distribute keystores to client devs and prepare a testnet config/genesis (mainnet-like config, 16k validators). Proto will try to host a stable main deployment (~10 nodes, ~2/3 validators), remaining keystores can be used for block-proposal testing by client devs. Connect nodes on Monday, start chain on Tuesday.
